headline: Mechanistic and causal models couple multimodal omics to cell-level biophysical dynamics
label: Mechanistic Omics Modeling
summary: Multimodal omics now feed explicit biophysical, signaling, and causal models that infer cell-type-resolved mechanisms in disease and aging.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inference of cell-level behavior from omics data under explicit mechanistic constraints. Probability flow matching learns biophysically consistent stochastic gene-regulatory dynamics from time-resolved data, while HMCVelo applies a deterministic ODE velocity framework to methylation and hydroxymethylation dynamics in single cells. Model-based calibration appears in a proteome-calibrated ODE digital twin of glioblastoma astrocyte signaling and in a multiscale framework coupling DPD membrane simulations, a systems signaling model, and PINN/PIKAN inference for macrophage RBC clearance. Other items pursue deconvolution or statistical integration: Celestial separates cell-type-specific aging changes from bulk spleen proteomes and transcriptomes, scVIP links single-cell expression to donor phenotypes, and a causal framework on a Cosserat scaffold ranks disease genes differently from association rankings. What is new is the coupling of biophysical and causal modeling with multimodal omics.
